text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Hosted API p99 latency spike + large request queue growth in us-west-2. Queue length trending up: 11.8k -> 14.3k in last 5m, 5xx rate + client timeouts. Auto-escalate to P1. :fire:
Maya (oncall): ack. I'm on it — paging infra leads. Observability shows GPU pool utilization at 98% and autoscaler stuck in 'scaling_queued'.
AJ: seeing the same. Provisioner logs show repeated 429s from cloud provider when creating instances. snippet:```HTTP 429 CreateInstances RateLimitExceeded retry-after: 120```
Liam: ops-provisioner is failing to reconcile new nodes. Looks like quota + provider-side rate limiting. Autoscaler keeps queueing scale actions but can't actually provision.
Nisha: customer visible impact? Any major customers timing out?
Maya (oncall): yes, a few high-QPS tenants hit timeouts; we have elevated error budgets for two mid-market customers. Routing shows traffic concentrated on a handful of model routes (text-gen-large) — heavy short-lived requests.
AJ: temporary mitigation idea: shift non-critical traffic to a smaller model variant (text-gen-medium) via routing weight adjustments, and enable token-based rate limiting for bursty API keys. Can do that from console.
Liam: agree. Also we can drop background batch jobs queued for <24h and free capacity.
Maya (oncall): I'll apply routing weight change now, 80/20 fallback to text-gen-medium for non-SLAd customers. Doing canary on 5% first.
Maya (oncall): /rollout route=text-gen-large fallback=text-gen-medium weight=0.05  <-- console command output: "rollout started, canary 5%"
ops-bot: NOTE: Provisioner rate-limit persists. Recent errors: ```ERR provisioner: create_instance failed: RateLimitExceeded (provider quota 100/hour)```
AJ: If we hit provider quota, we should also trigger cross-region fallback. Can we route new requests to eu-west-1 and us-east-1 where pools are below 70%?
Nisha: cross-region means added latency for some customers. Might be acceptable for lower-tier. We need to flag enterprise customers before moving them.
Liam: I'll open a fast permission to push cross-region weight for non-enterprise tenants. Patch ready: ```route_policy.apply(scope=non_enterprise, region_fallback=[us-east-1, eu-west-1], max_extra_latency=80ms)```
Maya (oncall): executing. Also enabling aggressive prefix-KV cache hits to reduce tokens generated per request.
Maya (oncall): cache warming toggle ON for routes text-gen-large,text-gen-medium.
deploy-bot: Deploy accepted: routing changes propagated to edge in ~30s.
AJ: rolling out token-based soft-shed for heavy API keys: keys above burst QPS=120 will receive 429 with Retry-After header for 30s — targeted to the top 10 offending keys.
Nisha: documenting customer impact and outreach plan. We need to notify the two affected customers now and offer prioritized request replay once healthy.
Maya (oncall): creating incident ticket INC-2026-453 and assigning to infra + oncall. Brief: autoscaler blocked by provider rate limits; mitigation = routing fallback, cross-region shift for non-enterprise, soft-shed on heavy keys.
AJ: quick check: any sign of autoscaler entering backoff loop? logs: ```autoscaler: state=scaling_queued attempts=6 last_error=RateLimitExceeded backoff=45s```
Liam: we've hit provider-side quota window (100/hour) — new node requests will be denied until window resets unless quota raised. Eng infra to request emergency quota bump.
Maya (oncall): @AJ can you escalate to cloud-ops to request quota bump and check if soft-limit can be temporarily increased?
AJ: on it. Opening cloud provider support case (case 987654321). ETA for reply unknown. Also sending internal override request.
ops-bot: ACTION LOGGED: cloud support case 987654321 created.
Nisha: customer comms draft: "We're experiencing elevated latency due to capacity constraints caused by a provider provisioning limit. We're routing non-critical traffic to alternate model variants/regions; enterprise customers unaffected by cross-region move unless notified. We'll follow up with timeline."
Maya (oncall): good. Postmortem owners? Suggest Liam + AJ + Nisha.
Liam: fine. Will dig into why autoscaler didn't fallback earlier to smaller instances / preemptible capacity.
AJ: will follow up on provisioner retries and add jitter to avoid synchronized bursts.
Nisha: will coordinate customer outreach and SLA credits if needed.
Maya (oncall): current metrics after fixes: queue length down to 6.1k, p95 improved from 18s -> 7.2s, p99 from 42s -> 19s. Still above normal but stabilizing.
AJ: hold for cloud provider update. If quota remains, plan B is to spin up smaller GPU types in another region and enable cross-cluster KV cache replication.
deploy-bot: routing rollback available if we need to restore original weighting.
Maya (oncall): keeping this thread open. If anyone sees new 5xx spikes push to #incidents-alerts and call the P1 bridge. Thanks for quick responses. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P1 created INC-2026-453. Paging: infra-lead, oncall, cloud-ops.
Maya (oncall): handoff in 45m to night oncall — documenting actions taken: routing canary -> 5% fallback, expanded to 25% after no regressions, cross-region for non-enterprise at 15%, soft-shed top keys, cache-warm enabled.
Liam: leaving logs and runbook notes in the ticket. Will investigate autoscaler thresholds that prevented earlier scale-up (min_pool_size override bug).
AJ: will add improved monitoring alerts for provisioner 429 rate and autoscaler 'scaling_queued' state.
Nisha: prepping external post-incident note for customers once root cause confirmed.
Maya (oncall): thanks team — I'll update status in 30m or earlier if cloud quota moves.
